messages.subject: Horizontal Lines along Y-axis for geom_bar plots
parts:
Dear List,


My code is producing the expected results - geom_bar. But, from my
read of "ggplot2" by Hadley Wickham and the available online
resources, I could not figure out which theme elements to use in opts
()

1) to draw horizontal lines from y-axis (but no vertical lines), and
2) to increase the font size and face bold of the "ylab".


Any help will be highly appreciated.

Thanks in advance.


Pradip Muhuri




# The code is shown below#
setwd ("F:/Disorders")
#setwd ("C:/Documents and Settings/pradip.muhuri/My Documents")
library (ggplot2)

myPlot <- function(lFrame,yTrigger )
{
lFrame$yvar = rep(c(0),21)
lFrame$yvar_l = rep(c(0),21)
lFrame$yvar_u = rep(c(0),21)
title =" "
outFile = "default.png"

if (yTrigger == 1)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$sumyr
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$sumyr_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$sumyr_u
title ="Past-Year Illicit Drug Use (2002-2010)"
outFile = "sumyr_race.png"
}

else if (yTrigger == 2)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$abodill
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$abodill_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$abodill_u
title ="Past-Year Illicit Drug Use Disorder (2002-2010)"
outFile = "abodill_race.png"
}

else if (yTrigger == 3)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$mrjyr
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$mrjyr_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$mrjyr_u
title ="Past-Year Marijuana Use (2002-2010)"
outFile = "mrjyr_race.png"
}

else if (yTrigger == 4)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$abodmrj
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$abodmrj_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$abodmrj_u
title ="Past-Year Marijuana Use Disorder (2002-2010)"
outFile = "abodmrj_race.png"
}


else if (yTrigger == 5)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$anlyr
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$anlyr_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$anlyr_u
title ="Past-Year Pain Reliever Use (2002-2010)"
outFile = "anlyr_race.png"
}


else if (yTrigger == 6)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$abodanl
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$abodanl_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$abodanl_u
title ="Past-Year Pain Reliever Use Disorder (2002-2010)"
outFile = "abodanl_race.png"
}

else if (yTrigger == 7)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$inhyr
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$inhyr_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$inhyr_u
title ="Past-Year Inhalant Use (2002-2010)"
outFile = "inhyr_race.png"
}


else if (yTrigger == 8)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$abodinh
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$abodinh_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$abodinh_u
title ="Past-Year Inhalant Use Disorder (2002-2010)"
outFile = "abodinh_race.png"
}

else if (yTrigger == 9)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$cocyr
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$cocyr_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$cocyr_u
title ="Past-Year Cocaine Use (2002-2010)"
outFile = "cocyr_race.png"
}

else if (yTrigger == 10)
{
lFrame$yvar = lFrame$abodcoc
lFrame$yvar_l = lFrame$abodcoc_l
lFrame$yvar_u = lFrame$abodcoc_u
title ="Past-Year Cocacine Use Disorder (2002-2010)"
outFile = "abodcoc_race.png"
}


lFrame$age <- factor(lFrame$age,
labels=c("12-17", "18-25", "26 or Older")
)

# In the data frame, race/ethnicity is coded as follows:
# 1=White, 2=Black, 3=AI/AN, 4="Hawiian/OPI",
# 5=Asian, 6=Multi Races,7=Hispanic


lFrame$race <- factor(lFrame$race,
levels=c
(5,2,4,7,1,6,3),
labels=c("Asian","Black","Hawiian/OPI",
"Hispanic",
"White","Multi Race","AI/AN"))
limits <- aes(ymax = yvar_u, ymin=yvar_l)
dodge <- position_dodge(width=1)

p <- ggplot(lFrame, aes(y=yvar, x=race, fill=race ))+
geom_bar(position=dodge) +
geom_errorbar(limits, position=dodge, width=0.3) +
#geom_text (aes(label = abodmrj,colour="black", face="bold"))
+
facet_wrap(~ age, ncol=3)+
scale_fill_manual(values=c("skyblue", "grey",
"orange","green", "yellow", "purple", "red")
)+
#ylim (0,16) +
xlab("")+
ylab("Percentages")+
opts(legend.position="none",
panel.grid.major = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(),
title=title,
axis.text.y=theme_text(size=16, face="bold"),
axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=90, hjust=1, size=16,
face="bold"),
panel.background=theme_rect(),
plot.title = theme_text(size=24, face="bold")
)


print (p)
ggsave(file=outFile, width=11, height=7)

}

load("rdframe1.rdata")

myPlot(rdframe1, 1)

parts:
Hi:

Here's an example: [note *both* code and data, which makes it reproducible]

dd <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10)
ggplot(dd, aes(x, y)) + theme_bw() +
ylab('My y label') +
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(face = 'bold', size = 16, angle = 90)) +
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank(), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank()) +
scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 10, by = 2)) +
geom_hline(aes(yintercept = seq(0, 10, by = 2)), colour = 'gray80') +
geom_point()

Theme elements (opts) are discussed in Chapter 8 of the ggplot2 book
by Hadley Wickham. axis.title.y is associated with aspects of the
y-axis title, panel.major.grid and panel.minor.grid with the major and
minor axis grid lines, respectively. In the current version, you need
to turn off the grid lines in both directions, but I believe in the
upcoming version, one will have the ability to exert more control over
individual grid directions. Corrections welcome if this is an
inaccurate statement.

But for now, the game is to turn of all grid lines, set the locations
where you want to replace them, and then replace them. That is the
purpose of the three lines preceding the geom_point() call.

HTH,
Dennis
